note: 'After that, Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said' (Exod 5:1). Aaron is given him as a mouth at 4:14-16 because Moses says he is not eloquent.

'And the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush ... God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses' (Exod 3:2-4).; 'And the LORD showed him the whole land' (Deut 34:1), and named the men he had sworn it to: 'This is the land that I swore to give Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob' (34:4). **The promise is closed by showing it to a man who may not enter.**; 'the angel of the LORD appeared to him in a blazing fire from within a bush' (Exod 3:2).; 'the angel of the LORD appeared to him in a blazing fire from within a bush' (Exod 3:2), and God called out of it at 3:4.

'Why are you crying out to Me? Tell the Israelites to go forward: lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea' (Exod 14:15-16), and again at 14:26 to bring the water back.; 'Behold, the time of your death is near. Call Joshua and present yourselves at the Tent of Meeting' (Deut 31:14), and the instruction to write the song at 31:19.; 'Go down at once, for your people, whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves' (Exod 32:7). **your people, whom you brought up** -- and Moses gives the words straight back at 32:11: 'your people, whom you brought out of Egypt'.; 'speak to the rock while they watch' (Num 20:8), and the reckoning at 20:12.
'Therefore, go! I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring My people the Israelites out of Egypt.' (Exod 3:10).
'God said to Moses, I AM WHO I AM.' (Exod 3:14), answering the question asked in the verse before.

'Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh' (Exod 3:11), and then the question that gets the answer: 'Suppose I go to the Israelites ... What is His name?’ What should I tell them?' (3:13).; 'The sight was so terrifying that even Moses said, I am trembling with fear.' (Heb 12:21). **Hebrews attributes a sentence to him that the Exodus account does not contain**, which the graph records as Hebrews reports it rather than smoothing over.; 'O LORD, why does Your anger burn against Your people' (Exod 32:11), and at the end of it an offer: 'Yet now, if You would only forgive their sin.... But if not, please blot me out of the book that You have written' (32:32). **The sentence breaks off unfinished in the middle**, which the KJV keeps.; 'So Moses cried out to the LORD, O God, please heal her!' (Num 12:13) -- five words for the man just complained against.; 'Pardon, I pray, the iniquity of this people, in keeping with the greatness of Your loving devotion' (Num 14:19), answered 'I have pardoned them as you requested,” the LORD replied' (14:20). **He argues from the formula of Exodus 34:6-7**, quoting it back at 14:18, which is one of the six places it travels.
'This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Let My people go, so that they may hold a feast to Me in the wilderness.' (Exod 5:1), repeated through the plagues.

'Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and all that night the LORD drove back the sea with a strong east wind' (Exod 14:21). **The verse divides the act between them** -- Moses stretches, the Lord drives -- and 14:31 names both again: 'the people feared the LORD and believed in Him and in His servant Moses'.; 'all those Moses led out of Egypt'. The verse names Moses and Egypt but not the people, who appear only as 'them that came out'.

'And the LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt so that he pursued the Israelites' (Exod 14:8). **Who hardened his heart is a question the book answers both ways** -- the Lord at 4:21, 7:3, 9:12 and here; Pharaoh himself at 8:15, 8:32 and 9:34 -- and the graph records the verses rather than choosing.

'You shall no longer supply the people with straw for making bricks. They must go and gather their own straw' (Exod 5:7), the tale of bricks unchanged (5:8). **The first result of asking is that it gets worse.**
